senses.gloss: To make fun of someone harshly, especially in front of an audience.
examples: His friends *roast* him about that haircut every single year.
The comedian *roasted* the mayor for twenty minutes.
She got *roasted* in the comments for that post.

senses.gloss: To take away from someone something they need or deserve.
examples: Don't let fear *rob* you of this chance.
A knee injury *robbed* him of his best years.
The players felt *robbed* of a fair result.

senses.gloss: To shake something hard, or to shock a group of people badly.
examples: Aftershocks *rock* the valley every few hours.
The scandal *rocked* the school board.
The whole building was *rocked* by the blast.

senses.gloss: To wrap or shape something into a tube or a ball.
senses.ru: скатывать, скатать; сворачивать, свернуть (в рулон, в трубочку)
examples: *Roll* the dough into small balls.
He *rolled* the poster carefully and slid it into a tube.
She was *rolling* tortillas while the beans cooked.

senses.gloss: To take turns doing something, or to change things in a fixed order.
examples: The nurses *rotate* between the day shift and the night shift.
We *rotated* the chores every week.
Farmers have *rotated* these crops for generations.

senses.gloss: To go around a corner, a bend, or the edge of something.
examples: *Round* the next bend and you will see the lake.
A truck *rounded* the corner too fast and clipped the mirror.
He was *rounding* third base when the throw came in.

senses.gloss: To upset someone's calm or annoy them slightly.
senses.ru: смущать, смутить; выводить из себя; задевать, задеть
examples: Tough questions never *ruffle* her.
The comment clearly *ruffled* the coach.
He looked a little *ruffled* when they asked about the money.

senses.gloss: To have power over a country or a people and govern them.
examples: Few kings *rule* without an army behind them.
She *ruled* the region for nearly thirty years.
The same family has *ruled* the island since 1890.

senses.gloss: To move suddenly toward someone or something in order to attack or take it.
senses.ru: бросаться, броситься (на); идти на штурм, штурмовать
examples: Fans *rush* the field every time the team wins at home.
Two men *rushed* the stage before security caught them.
The crowd was *rushing* the gates an hour before the doors opened.

senses.gloss: To rob and destroy a captured town or building.
examples: Invading armies usually *sack* the capital first.
The soldiers *sacked* the village and burned the fields.
Rome was *sacked* in 410.

senses.gloss: To kill an animal or a person as an offering to a god.
senses.ru: приносить в жертву, принести в жертву
examples: Some cultures still *sacrifice* an animal at harvest time.
The priests *sacrificed* a goat each spring.
The lamb was *sacrificed* on the altar.

senses.gloss: To give someone a difficult job, debt, or responsibility they did not want.
examples: Don't *saddle* the new guy with all the paperwork.
The deal *saddled* the company with huge debts.
Many graduates are *saddled* with loans for decades.

senses.gloss: To move smoothly and easily through the air or across a space.
examples: Fly balls *sail* out of that park all summer.
The ball *sailed* over the fence and into the parking lot.
A paper plane came *sailing* past my desk.

senses.gloss: To take a short piece of an existing recording and use it in a new song.
examples: Producers still *sample* old soul records.
The chorus *sampled* a bass line from 1972.
That drum break has been *sampled* hundreds of times.

senses.gloss: To give official permission or approval for something.
examples: The city will not *sanction* a march without a permit.
The league *sanctioned* the event and sent officials.
Only races *sanctioned* by the federation count for points.

senses.gloss: To remove the parts of a story or a document that might offend or reveal too much.
examples: Textbooks often *sanitize* the ugliest parts of the war.
The agency *sanitized* the report before releasing it.
We only got a *sanitized* version of what happened that night.

senses.gloss: To meet a requirement, a condition, or a standard.
examples: Two lab courses *satisfy* the science requirement.
The design *satisfied* every safety rule.
He has *satisfied* all the conditions of his parole.

senses.gloss: To take someone or something out of danger.
examples: Seat belts *save* thousands of lives a year.
A neighbor *saved* the dog from the flooded yard.
He was *saved* by a passing fishing boat.

senses.gloss: To store a computer file so that you can use it later.
examples: *Save* the file before you close the laptop.
I *saved* the photos to a flash drive.
The document had not been *saved*, and an hour of work was gone.

senses.gloss: To make it unnecessary for someone to spend time or effort.
examples: Taking the express will *save* you an hour.
One phone call *saved* us a trip downtown.
You could have *saved* yourself a lot of trouble by asking first.

senses.gloss: To climb up something high and steep.
examples: Few climbers *scale* that face in winter.
They *scaled* the fence in about three seconds.
She has *scaled* every major peak in the state.

senses.gloss: To pass something through a machine that reads it or makes a digital copy.
examples: Please *scan* your boarding pass at the gate.
The clerk *scanned* every item twice.
All the old letters have been *scanned* and backed up.

senses.gloss: To harm someone emotionally in a way that lasts for years.
examples: Losing a parent young can *scar* a child for life.
The divorce *scarred* both of them.
He came home *scarred* by what he had seen overseas.

senses.gloss: To manage to get something you want, often by luck (informal).
examples: He always *scores* the best seats somehow.
We *scored* two tickets an hour before the show.
She had *scored* an interview with the director.

senses.gloss: To write the music for a film, a show, or a game.
examples: He *scores* two or three films a year.
A jazz trio *scored* the whole series.
The movie was *scored* by a first-time composer.

senses.gloss: To cut shallow lines into a surface.
examples: *Score* the bread before it goes into the oven.
He *scored* the drywall and snapped it along the line.
The fat is *scored* so that it renders evenly.

senses.gloss: To search a place or a list very thoroughly.
examples: Volunteers *scour* the beach after every storm.
We *scoured* three stores looking for that part.
They have *scoured* every record in the archive.

senses.gloss: To go and look over a place in advance in order to find something or learn what is there.
examples: We should *scout* the trail before we bring the kids.
She *scouted* four cities before choosing one for the store.
A small team was *scouting* locations for the shoot.

senses.gloss: To move or act in a hurry, often climbing or struggling to get somewhere.
examples: Kids *scramble* over those rocks all day long.
He *scrambled* up the bank to reach the road.
Teams are *scrambling* to sign a backup goalie.

senses.gloss: To mix up a signal or a message so that it cannot be understood without special equipment.
examples: Cheap radios don't *scramble* anything.
The station *scrambled* the broadcast for paying subscribers.
Their calls were *scrambled*, so no one could listen in.

senses.gloss: To remove a layer from a surface by pulling something hard or sharp across it.
examples: I *scrape* the frost from the windshield every morning.
She *scraped* the burned cheese from the pan.
The old paint has been *scraped* down to bare wood.

senses.gloss: To cancel something that was planned, or to remove a name from a list.
examples: *Scratch* that idea; let's meet on Friday instead.
They *scratched* the horse the morning of the race.
Two names have been *scratched* from the program.

senses.gloss: To make a harsh, high sound, as tires or brakes do.
examples: The old brakes *screech* every time he stops.
A car *screeched* to a halt at the curb.
The subway came *screeching* into the station.

senses.gloss: To show a film or a program to an audience.
examples: The theater *screens* old westerns on Sunday nights.
They *screened* the documentary for the crew first.
The film has been *screened* at three festivals.

senses.gloss: To check people or things in order to decide which ones to let through.
examples: They *screen* every applicant before the interview.
Security *screened* all the bags at the door.
He was *screening* his calls all week.

senses.gloss: To hide or protect something from view, light, or wind.
senses.ru: заслонять, заслонить; закрывать (от вида, света); отгораживать
examples: Tall hedges *screen* the yard from the road.
A row of pines *screened* the house from the highway.
The patio is *screened* from the wind by a stone wall.

senses.gloss: To cancel something that was planned, especially at the last minute.
examples: They may *scrub* the launch if the wind picks up.
The airline *scrubbed* the flight because of ice on the wings.
The mission was *scrubbed* twice in one week.

senses.gloss: To run with short, quick steps, the way a crab or a mouse does.
examples: Crabs *scuttle* sideways into the wet sand.
A mouse *scuttled* under the stove.
We watched a lizard go *scuttling* across the path.

senses.gloss: To sink a ship on purpose by letting water into it.
examples: A captain may *scuttle* a ship rather than hand it over.
The crew *scuttled* the boat in shallow water.
The old freighter was *scuttled* to make an artificial reef.

senses.gloss: To make something final and certain.
examples: A handshake will *seal* the agreement.
That free throw *sealed* the win.
His fate was *sealed* the moment the tape turned up.

senses.gloss: To examine a person, a vehicle, or a place thoroughly to find something hidden.
examples: Officers may not *search* your car without cause.
They *searched* the apartment for two hours.
Every bag is *searched* at the entrance.

senses.gloss: To have enough seats for a particular number of people.
examples: The hall *seats* about four hundred people.
The original stadium *seated* only twenty thousand.
Once the patio is finished, the restaurant will *seat* ninety.

senses.gloss: To get something important after effort or negotiation.
examples: The team is trying to *secure* funding for another year.
She *secured* a spot in the program on her second try.
They have *secured* enough votes to pass the bill.

senses.gloss: To make a place or a system safe from attack or from being broken into.
senses.ru: обеспечивать безопасность, защищать, защитить; брать под охрану
examples: You should *secure* the network before the office opens.
Troops *secured* the airport within a day.
The site has been *secured*, and nobody gets in without a badge.

senses.gloss: To rank players or teams before a tournament so that the best ones do not meet early.
senses.ru: сеять, посеять (в турнирной сетке); распределять по посеву
examples: The committee will *seed* the teams on Sunday.
They *seeded* her second despite the injury.
He is *seeded* fourth in his half of the draw.

senses.gloss: To take the seeds out of a fruit or a vegetable.
senses.ru: вынимать семена, очищать от семян (перец, помидоры)
examples: *Seed* the peppers before you slice them.
He *seeded* and chopped four tomatoes.
The jalapeños should be *seeded* if you want less heat.

senses.gloss: To stop living together as a couple without being divorced yet.
examples: Couples who *separate* often still share the kids' schedule.
They *separated* last spring after eleven years.
He has been *separated* from his wife since March.

senses.gloss: To be the quality that makes one person or thing different from another.
examples: Attention to detail *separates* a good cook from a great one.
One point *separated* the two teams at the buzzer.
The finalists were *separated* by less than a second.

senses.gloss: To work out the exact order of the parts of a gene or a genome.
examples: Labs can now *sequence* a whole genome in a day.
Researchers *sequenced* the virus within weeks.
The sample has been *sequenced* twice to be sure.

senses.gloss: To be used as something, or to be useful for a purpose.
examples: An old door *serves* as our kitchen table.
The gym *served* as a shelter during the storm.
That hallway has *served* as a gallery for years.

senses.gloss: To spend a period of time in prison or in the armed forces.
examples: He will *serve* eighteen months.
She *served* two tours overseas.
He has *served* most of his sentence already.

senses.gloss: In tennis or volleyball, to put the ball into play by hitting it.
examples: She *serves* harder than anyone else on the tour.
He *served* four aces in one game.
He was *serving* for the match when the rain started.

senses.gloss: To provide a service to a place or a group of people.
examples: Two airlines *service* the island.
The bus route *serviced* four towns before it was cut.
The whole county is *serviced* by a single clinic.

senses.gloss: To go to live in a place and stay there.
examples: Many families *settle* here for the schools.
Her grandparents *settled* in Chicago in 1951.
The valley was *settled* long before the railroad came.

senses.gloss: To sink slowly and come to rest at the bottom or on a surface.
examples: Let the grounds *settle* before you pour the coffee.
Dust *settled* on every surface after the drywall work.
Sand has *settled* at the bottom of the jar.

senses.gloss: To end a connection or a relationship completely.
examples: The two countries may *sever* diplomatic ties.
The company *severed* its relationship with the supplier.
All contact with the group has been *severed*.

senses.gloss: To keep sunlight off something by blocking the light.
examples: Two big oaks *shade* the whole backyard.
She *shaded* her eyes with one hand and looked up.
The tables are *shaded* by wide umbrellas.

senses.gloss: To follow someone closely and secretly in order to watch what they do.
senses.ru: следить (за кем-л.), ходить по пятам; вести слежку
examples: Two agents *shadow* him whenever he leaves the hotel.
A detective *shadowed* her for a week.
He realized he was being *shadowed* by the same gray car.
